# DividendBro

> DividendBro is a free dividend tracker for US, Canadian (TSX), and Singapore (SGX) stocks. Track real-time dividend yields, ex-dividend payout dates, dividend calendars, payout ratios, and monthly income projections across 670+ securities. Includes a portfolio tracker, dividend screener, and stock comparison tool. Educational tool only — not financial advice.

DividendBro covers 672 dividend-paying securities across US, Canadian, and Singapore markets, including stocks, REITs, ETFs, bond ETFs, and preferred stocks. All data is sourced from Yahoo Finance and Financial Modeling Prep.

## Main Tools

- [Monthly Dividend Income Planner](https://dividendbro.com/): Enter a target monthly dividend income and see a sample allocation for US, Canadian, or SGX markets (or a blend of all three), filtered by risk appetite.
- [Dividend Screener](https://dividendbro.com/screener): Browse 672 dividend-paying stocks by payout frequency (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly), asset type (stocks, REITs, ETFs, bond ETFs, preferred stocks), and risk level. Supports US, Canadian, and SGX markets.
- [Stock Search](https://dividendbro.com/search): Look up any US, Canadian (TSX), or SGX ticker for dividend history, yield, payout ratio, dividend CAGR, and safety score.
- [Stock Comparison](https://dividendbro.com/compare): Compare up to 5 dividend stocks side-by-side on yield, payout ratio, dividend CAGR, streak, and total return.
- [Millionaire Simulator](https://dividendbro.com/millionaire): Project how long a fixed monthly investment takes to reach $1,000,000 in a given dividend stock with or without DRIP. Includes a quality-filtered leaderboard of dividend compounders.
- [DCA Simulator](https://dividendbro.com/simulate/dca): Simulate dollar-cost averaging into a dividend stock with monthly contributions and dividend reinvestment.
- [One-Time Investment Simulator](https://dividendbro.com/simulate/one-time): Calculate total historical return on a lump-sum dividend stock investment including dividends.

- [Weekly Dividend ETFs](https://dividendbro.com/weekly-dividend-etfs): Complete list of 73 weekly dividend ETFs, their issuers (YieldMax, Roundhill, Defiance, GraniteShares), and the return-of-capital risks behind the headline yields.
- [Monthly Dividend Stocks](https://dividendbro.com/monthly-dividend-stocks): Full list of 133 monthly dividend payers — REITs, BDCs, closed-end funds, and covered-call ETFs.
- [REITs That Pay Monthly](https://dividendbro.com/reits-that-pay-monthly): The verified 2026 list of US REITs paying monthly dividends, with cadence changes and tax treatment for Singapore investors.
- [Top Dividend Stocks](https://dividendbro.com/top): Highest-yielding dividend stocks and ETFs in the US, Canadian, and SGX markets, ranked by trailing yield.

## FAQ

**What is a dividend tracker?**
A dividend tracker is a tool that monitors your dividend income, yield, ex-dividend dates, and payout history across your portfolio. DividendBro is a free dividend tracker covering 670+ stocks across US, SGX, and TSX markets.

**What does DividendBro do?**
DividendBro is a free dividend tracker for US, Canadian, and SGX markets. It tracks dividend history, yield, payout dates, dividend growth, and safety metrics for 672 securities across stocks, REITs, ETFs, bond ETFs, and preferred stocks.

**Is DividendBro free?**
Yes. All features are free — no paywall, no subscription, no credit card required. Basic stock analysis doesn't even require sign-up.

**Does DividendBro cover Singapore stocks?**
Yes. SGX stocks including DBS, OCBC, UOB, Singtel, Singapore Airlines, and all major S-REITs are covered alongside US and Canadian markets.

**Does DividendBro cover Canadian stocks?**
Yes. 29 TSX-listed dividend stocks are covered, including the Big Six banks (RBC, TD, Scotiabank, BMO, CIBC, National Bank), major pipelines (Enbridge, TC Energy, Pembina, Suncor), telecoms (BCE, Telus), utilities (Fortis, Canadian Utilities), and Canadian REITs (SmartCentres, RioCan, Granite, Choice Properties). The screener, income planner, and stock detail pages all support the Canadian market.

**How much do I need to invest to make $1,000 a month in dividends?**
To earn $1,000 per month ($12,000 per year) in dividends, you generally need to invest between $150,000 and $200,000, depending on your portfolio's average yield. Use DividendBro's income planner to simulate exact monthly income based on your SGX and US holdings.

**Which stocks in Singapore pay the highest dividends?**
DBS, OCBC, and UOB are highly popular among Singapore investors for stable yields. DividendBro tracks their exact ex-dividend dates, dividend yield, and full payout history.

**What is an ex-dividend date?**
The ex-dividend date is the cutoff date to be a shareholder of record to receive the next dividend. Buy on or after this date and you won't receive that dividend. DividendBro shows upcoming ex-dividend dates for every stock it tracks.

**What's the difference between weekly and monthly dividend ETFs?**
Weekly dividend ETFs are almost entirely options-income strategies that sell call options and pass the premium to shareholders. Distributions often include return of capital. Monthly dividend stocks include REITs, BDCs, and closed-end funds that pay from actual business income — a more traditional income category.

**Which REITs pay monthly dividends?**
Realty Income (O), Agree Realty (ADC), LTC Properties (LTC), EPR Properties (EPR), Healthpeak (DOC), Apple Hospitality (APLE), Gladstone Commercial (GOOD), and AGNC Investment (AGNC) are among the ~19 US-listed REITs that pay monthly in 2026.

**Are there daily dividend stocks?**
SATA (Strive Bitcoin-backed preferred stock) and CHAD (DeFi Development Solana-backed preferred stock) are the only two live daily dividend payers. Four more from Strategy (STRC, STRF, STRK, STRD) are pending shareholder approval in October 2026.

**How are Canadian dividends taxed for non-residents?**
Canada imposes a 25% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents, reduced to 15% under most tax treaties (including US, UK, Singapore, Australia). The tax is withheld at source and cannot be reclaimed by filing a Canadian return.

**What is a TFSA and why does it matter for dividend investors?**
The Tax-Free Savings Account (TFSA) is a Canadian registered account where Canadian dividends are 100% tax-free. The 2026 annual contribution limit is $7,000, with cumulative room of $109,000 for eligible Canadians who have never contributed. This is the single biggest tax advantage available to Canadian dividend investors.

**What is the SGX board lot change of 2026?**
Effective October 5, 2026, SGX reduced board lot sizes for 11 major stocks. Stocks priced S$10–S$100 now trade in lots of 10 shares (down from 100). Stocks above S$100 trade in lots of 1 share. The reduced lot sizes are permanent. Affected stocks include DBS, OCBC, UOB, SGX, Great Eastern, Jardine Matheson, Jardine C&C, Haw Par, Venture Corp, Prudential, and Keppel (Keppel kept 100-share lots since it trades below S$10).

**Can I buy just 1 share of DBS on SGX?**
No. DBS is priced between S$10 and S$100, so its board lot size is 10 shares. You can only buy 1 share of stocks priced above S$100.

**Does DividendBro give financial advice?**
No. DividendBro is an educational tool. It is not licensed under the Financial Advisers Act (Singapore) and is not a registered investment adviser in the US. All content and tools are for informational purposes only.

**What data sources does DividendBro use?**
Dividend history and prices come from Yahoo Finance. Payout ratios come from Financial Modeling Prep (US-listed only). Visitor geography is derived from Cloudflare's CF-IPCountry header. All data is provided "as is."
